items.q: According to Carroll's pyramid of corporate social responsibility, which of the following correctly ranks the four levels from the base of the pyramid to the top?
opts: Economic, legal, ethical, philanthropic
Legal, economic, ethical, philanthropic
Economic, ethical, legal, philanthropic
Philanthropic, ethical, legal, economic
items.why: Carroll places economic responsibilities at the base (the foundation without which the business cannot exist), followed by legal, then ethical, then philanthropic at the top. Students commonly swap the order of legal and ethical, or place philanthropic at the bottom because they associate CSR primarily with charitable giving.
items.label: New question

items.q:
Which of the following best illustrates how changing social attitudes can create a business opportunity?

Statement 1: Growing consumer concern about single-use plastic has led some food retailers to introduce packaging-free product lines.
Statement 2: Social change always forces businesses to reduce their product ranges.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Statement 1 is a clear example of social change driving product innovation and opening new markets. Statement 2 is false: social change can expand product ranges as well as contract them. Students sometimes treat external pressures as purely negative constraints rather than as sources of opportunity.
items.label: New question

items.q: Which one of these stakeholders is least likely to have their needs satisfied by a company?
opts: Competitors
Employees
Shareholders
Suppliers
items.why: Competitors are least likely to have needs satisfied because businesses actively compete against them. A company's success often comes at its competitors' expense. Competitors are stakeholders, but the business has no incentive to satisfy their needs.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Budget vs Actual: Revenue 26/28, Materials 8/9, Labour 12/10 (all £000). Which statement is true?
opts: Revenue has adverse variance
Material costs have favourable variance
Profits have favourable variance
Difference between budgeted and actual profit is £15,000
items.why: Budgeted profit = 26 - 8 - 12 = £6k. Actual profit = 28 - 9 - 10 = £9k. Actual profit (£9k) > Budget (£6k) = favourable variance of £3k. Calculate overall profit, not just individual items. Revenue up = favourable.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: In a SWOT analysis, which statement is true?
opts: A recession in the business's main export market is a weakness.
An increase in labour productivity is an opportunity.
An increase in the number of patents held by a business is a strength.
Disappointing R&D innovation levels are a threat.
items.why: Patents are an internal asset that gives competitive advantage, making them a strength. A recession is external (threat, not weakness). Productivity is internal (strength, not opportunity). Disappointing R&D is internal (weakness, not threat). SWOT rule: Internal = Strengths/Weaknesses. External = Opportunities/Threats.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Forecasting future sales by projecting past trends in sales is known as:
opts: Correlation
Extrapolation
Market mapping
Qualitative market research
items.why: Correlation measures relationships between variables. Market mapping plots brand positions. Correlation = measuring relationships between variables.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Greenway Engineering has a deeply embedded role culture with rigid departmental boundaries and a heavy reliance on written procedures. The company needs to adopt a more innovative, project-based way of working. Which of the following represents the most significant cultural barrier to this change?
opts: Employees are likely to have high levels of individual autonomy that conflict with team working
The organisation's focus on rules and hierarchy makes rapid, flexible responses difficult
The concentration of power in one individual means change depends entirely on that person's attitude
Employees prioritise their own professional development over organisational goals
items.why: Role culture is defined by rules, procedures and hierarchy, which create inflexibility — the opposite of the innovative, project-based culture required. Option C describes a power culture, not a role culture. Option A is associated with person culture, and option D does not reflect any of Handy's identified cultural characteristics.
items.label: New question

items.q: Current liabilities are 3x current assets. Shareholders provide 20% of capital employed. The business has:
opts: High current ratio and high gearing
High current ratio and low gearing
Low current ratio and high gearing
Low current ratio and low gearing
items.why: Current ratio = CA/CL. If CL is 3x CA, ratio is 0.33:1 = low. Gearing = non-current liabilities / capital employed x 100. If shareholders = 20%, then debt = 80% = high gearing. Shareholders' funds = equity. If equity is only 20%, the other 80% must be debt = very high gearing.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Based on Tannenbaum and Schmidt's continuum of leadership, in which part does the manager have least authority?
opts: Consult
Sell
Share/Joins
Tell
items.why: Share/Joins is the most democratic end where the manager has least authority. The order: Tell (most authority) > Sell > Consult > Share/Joins (least authority). 'Tell' = autocratic.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Which policy combination increases sales for a house builder?
opts: Decreasing interest rates and decreasing taxation
Decreasing interest rates and increasing taxation
Increasing interest rates and decreasing taxation
Increasing interest rates and increasing taxation
items.why: Lower interest rates: cheaper mortgages = more house buyers + lower borrowing costs for the builder. Lower taxation: consumers have more disposable income. Both boost housing demand. House builders are highly sensitive to interest rates (mortgages) and consumer spending power (taxation).
items.label: Past paper question

items.q:
An ageing population in the UK is likely to have which of the following effects on a business selling mobility aids?

Statement 1: The size of the target market for mobility aids will increase as the proportion of older people in the population grows.
Statement 2: An ageing population will reduce the size of the working-age labour supply available to the business.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Both statements are correct. A larger elderly cohort directly expands demand for mobility aids. An ageing population simultaneously shrinks the proportion of working-age people, tightening labour supply. Students often assume only the demand-side effect matters and overlook the labour-market consequence.
items.label: New question

items.q:
In Porter's five forces model, which of the following circumstances would most increase the bargaining power of suppliers to a manufacturer?

Statement 1: There are only two suppliers globally who can provide the specialist component the manufacturer needs.
Statement 2: The manufacturer's product accounts for 60% of each supplier's total revenue.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: A very small number of suppliers for a specialised input increases supplier power because the manufacturer has few alternatives. Statement 1 is therefore true. If the manufacturer represents 60% of a supplier's revenue, the supplier is heavily dependent on the manufacturer, which reduces — not increases — supplier power, so Statement 2 is false.
items.label: New question

items.q:
Nexo plc manufactures chemicals. It complies with all environmental regulations but refuses to adopt any voluntary environmental standards beyond the legal minimum, and it donates nothing to community projects.

Statement 1: Nexo plc is meeting its economic and legal responsibilities according to Carroll's pyramid.
Statement 2: Nexo plc is meeting its ethical and philanthropic responsibilities according to Carroll's pyramid.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Nexo is profitable (economic) and law-abiding (legal), so Statement 1 is true. Ethical responsibilities require going beyond the law to do what is right; philanthropic responsibilities involve contributing to the community. Nexo does neither, so Statement 2 is false.
items.label: New question

items.q: Ordinary shares traded on the stock exchange are those issued by:
opts: Private limited companies
Public limited companies
Public sector organisations
Sole traders
items.why: Only PLCs can trade shares on the stock exchange. Private limited companies cannot sell shares publicly. PLC = private sector, shares traded publicly.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Elkington's triple bottom line framework requires a business to report on which three dimensions of performance?
opts: Profit, productivity, and people
People, planet, and profit
Price, planet, and productivity
Profit, planet, and philanthropy
items.why: Elkington's triple bottom line consists of the three Ps: people (social), planet (environmental), and profit (economic). Students sometimes substitute 'philanthropy' or 'productivity' for one of the three Ps.
items.label: New question

items.q: Culture changes from decisions by the original owner to stated rules and defined responsibilities. According to Handy, this is:
opts: Person to role
Person to task
Power to role
Power to task
items.why: Original owner making all decisions = Power culture (centralised, one dominant figure). Stated rules and defined responsibilities = Role culture (bureaucratic, formal procedures). Change: Power to Role. Power culture = one person/small group controls everything. Role culture = formal rules, job descriptions, procedures.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q:
Vesta Foods publishes an annual report showing its carbon emissions, the wages paid relative to the living wage, and its net profit margin.

Statement 1: Vesta Foods is reporting against all three elements of Elkington's triple bottom line.
Statement 2: Elkington's triple bottom line argues that long-run financial performance is independent of a firm's social and environmental performance.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Carbon emissions cover 'planet', wages relative to the living wage cover 'people', and net profit margin covers 'profit', so Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false: Elkington's framework explicitly argues that sustainable long-run profit depends on social and environmental performance, not that the three are independent.
items.label: New question

items.q: Statement 1: 'External growth requires integration with a business in a different country.' Statement 2: 'Organic growth uses own resources to expand.'
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Statement 1 false: external growth can be domestic OR international - it just means merging/taking over another business. Statement 2 true: organic growth means expanding using the business's own resources (reinvesting profits, opening new stores, etc.). External growth doesn't require different countries. A UK firm buying another UK firm is still external growth.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Prestige Air is a small airline operating on a single domestic route. A large rival airline announces it will begin operating the same route next month. According to Porter's five forces, which force does this most directly represent?
opts: Threat of substitute products
Bargaining power of buyers
Threat of new entrants
Rivalry among existing competitors
items.why: A firm entering a market for the first time is a new entrant, even if it is large and established elsewhere. Students frequently confuse this with rivalry among existing competitors, but the rival is not yet operating on this route, so it represents the threat of entry rather than existing competitive rivalry.
items.label: New question

items.q: GreenRide is an electric scooter company. Having identified young urban commuters aged 18–30 as its target segment, it positions its brand around convenience and sustainability. Which targeting strategy is GreenRide most likely using?
opts: Undifferentiated targeting
Concentrated targeting
Differentiated targeting
Customised targeting
items.why: Concentrated (niche) targeting involves focusing all marketing effort on a single, clearly defined segment — which is what GreenRide is doing by focusing exclusively on young urban commuters. Undifferentiated targeting treats the whole market as one; differentiated targeting involves serving multiple segments with tailored mixes. Students sometimes confuse concentrated with differentiated because both involve defined segments.
items.label: New question
